name: Enhanced Due Diligence for High-Risk Customers
description: Policy mandating enhanced due diligence procedures for high-risk customers prior to account activation or exception approval. Establishes requirements for beneficial ownership verification, source of funds assessment, multi-source screening, and ongoing monitoring at elevated frequency.
context: A high-risk customer must receive enhanced due diligence before the account is activated or an exception is approved.
Enhanced Due Diligence for High-Risk Customers

name: Beneficial Ownership Identification and Verification
description: Requirement to identify and verify every beneficial owner of entity customers with more than 25% ownership or control. Applies to all high-risk entity customers undergoing enhanced due diligence.
context: For entity customers, identify and verify every beneficial owner with more than 25% ownership or control

name: Source of Funds Assessment for Initial Deposits
description: Requirement to obtain and assess evidence for initial deposits exceeding £10,000 from high-risk customers. Establishes a monetary threshold triggering enhanced source of funds documentation.
context: Obtain and assess evidence for an initial deposit above £10,000

name: Multi-Source Sanctions and PEP Screening
description: Requirement to screen high-risk customers against OFAC, EU, UN, HMT, PEP lists, sanctions databases, and adverse-media sources. Establishes the screening sources and scope for high-risk customer due diligence.
context: Screen OFAC, EU, UN, HMT, PEP, sanctions, and adverse-media sources

name: Head of Compliance Approval for Account Activation
description: Requirement that the Head of Compliance must approve account activation for high-risk customers after enhanced due diligence is completed. Establishes the approval gate and responsible role.
context: Head of Compliance approval before activation

name: Chief Risk Officer Approval for Policy Exceptions
description: Requirement that the Chief Risk Officer must approve any policy exception for high-risk customers. Establishes escalation authority for deviations from standard enhanced due diligence requirements.
context: CRO approval for any policy exception

name: Quarterly Ongoing Monitoring for High-Risk Customers
description: Requirement to review high-risk customers at least quarterly rather than annually. Establishes elevated monitoring frequency for high-risk customer accounts post-activation.
context: Review high-risk customers at least quarterly rather than annually

name: High-Risk Customer Status
description: Risk category identifying customers assessed as high-risk, requiring enhanced due diligence procedures, elevated screening, and ongoing monitoring. Triggers mandatory approval gates and quarterly review obligations.
context: A high-risk customer must receive enhanced due diligence before the account is activated or an exception is approved.
Review high-risk customers at least quarterly rather than annually

name: OFAC Sanctions Screening
description: Screening control against the Office of Foreign Assets Control sanctions list. Applied to high-risk customers as part of multi-source screening requirements.
context: Screen OFAC, EU, UN, HMT, PEP, sanctions, and adverse-media sources

name: EU Sanctions List Screening
description: Screening control against European Union sanctions lists. Applied to high-risk customers as part of multi-source screening requirements.
context: Screen OFAC, EU, UN, HMT, PEP, sanctions, and adverse-media sources

name: UN Sanctions List Screening
description: Screening control against United Nations sanctions lists. Applied to high-risk customers as part of multi-source screening requirements.
context: Screen OFAC, EU, UN, HMT, PEP, sanctions, and adverse-media sources

name: HMT Sanctions List Screening
description: Screening control against Her Majesty's Treasury sanctions lists. Applied to high-risk customers as part of multi-source screening requirements.
context: Screen OFAC, EU, UN, HMT, PEP, sanctions, and adverse-media sources

name: PEP List Screening
description: Screening control against Politically Exposed Person lists. Applied to high-risk customers as part of multi-source screening requirements.
context: Screen OFAC, EU, UN, HMT, PEP, sanctions, and adverse-media sources

name: Adverse Media Screening
description: Screening control against adverse media sources for reputational risk assessment. Applied to high-risk customers as part of multi-source screening requirements.
context: Screen OFAC, EU, UN, HMT, PEP, sanctions, and adverse-media sources

name: Head of Compliance
description: Role responsible for approving account activation for high-risk customers after enhanced due diligence completion. Holds authority to gate account opening based on compliance assessment.
context: Head of Compliance approval before activation

name: Chief Risk Officer
description: Role responsible for approving any policy exceptions for high-risk customers. Holds escalation authority for deviations from standard enhanced due diligence requirements.
context: CRO approval for any policy exception

name: High-Risk Customer
description: Customer classification requiring enhanced due diligence procedures prior to account activation. Subject to elevated screening, beneficial ownership verification, source of funds assessment, and quarterly ongoing monitoring.
context: A high-risk customer must receive enhanced due diligence before the account is activated or an exception is approved.
Review high-risk customers at least quarterly rather than annually

name: Enhanced Due Diligence Verification
description: Enhanced KYC verification process for high-risk customers encompassing beneficial ownership identification, source of funds assessment, and multi-source screening. Must be completed before account activation or exception approval.
context: A high-risk customer must receive enhanced due diligence before the account is activated or an exception is approved.
For entity customers, identify and verify every beneficial owner with more than 25% ownership or control

name: High-Risk Customer Screening
description: AML screening process for high-risk customers against multiple sanctions and PEP sources including OFAC, EU, UN, HMT lists, and adverse media. Mandatory component of enhanced due diligence.
context: Screen OFAC, EU, UN, HMT, PEP, sanctions, and adverse-media sources

name: Account Evidence and Escalation Policy
description: Policy governing the retention of account evidence, screening results, and risk documentation, with mandatory escalation procedures to Financial Crime for missing evidence, positive screening results, unclear ownership, or suspicious funds. Prohibits account activation pending resolution of flagged issues.
context: The account record must retain ownership and source-of-funds evidence, screening results, risk rating, approver, and review date.
Missing evidence, a positive screening result, unclear ownership, or suspicious funds must be referred to Financial Crime.
Staff must not activate the account while the issue is open.

name: Mandatory Account Record Evidence Retention
description: Requires that account records retain ownership evidence, source-of-funds evidence, screening results, risk rating, approver identity, and review date as a condition of account management.
context: The account record must retain ownership and source-of-funds evidence, screening results, risk rating, approver, and review date.

name: Escalation of Missing Evidence to Financial Crime
description: Mandates referral to Financial Crime when account evidence is missing, including ownership documentation or source-of-funds verification.
context: Missing evidence, a positive screening result, unclear ownership, or suspicious funds must be referred to Financial Crime.

name: Escalation of Positive Screening Results to Financial Crime
description: Requires immediate referral to Financial Crime when AML screening returns a positive result during account onboarding or review.
context: Missing evidence, a positive screening result, unclear ownership, or suspicious funds must be referred to Financial Crime.

name: Escalation of Unclear Ownership to Financial Crime
description: Mandates referral to Financial Crime when account ownership cannot be clearly established or verified.
context: Missing evidence, a positive screening result, unclear ownership, or suspicious funds must be referred to Financial Crime.

name: Escalation of Suspicious Funds to Financial Crime
description: Requires referral to Financial Crime when funds deposited to or held in an account are identified as suspicious or potentially illicit.
context: Missing evidence, a positive screening result, unclear ownership, or suspicious funds must be referred to Financial Crime.

name: Prohibition on Account Activation During Open Issues
description: Prohibits staff from activating or opening an account while evidence gaps, screening issues, ownership concerns, or suspicious fund investigations remain unresolved.
context: Staff must not activate the account while the issue is open.

name: Missing Account Evidence
description: Risk arising from incomplete or absent ownership documentation, source-of-funds verification, or other required account evidence, creating compliance and AML exposure.
context: Missing evidence, a positive screening result, unclear ownership, or suspicious funds must be referred to Financial Crime.

name: Positive AML Screening Result
description: Risk identified when AML screening (sanctions, PEP, or adverse media checks) returns a positive match or alert during account onboarding or periodic review.
context: Missing evidence, a positive screening result, unclear ownership, or suspicious funds must be referred to Financial Crime.

name: Unclear Account Ownership
description: Risk arising when the beneficial owner, legal owner, or signatory authority on an account cannot be clearly identified or verified.
context: Missing evidence, a positive screening result, unclear ownership, or suspicious funds must be referred to Financial Crime.

name: Suspicious Funds
description: Risk identified when funds deposited to or held in an account are suspected to be proceeds of crime, illicit activity, or money laundering.
context: Missing evidence, a positive screening result, unclear ownership, or suspicious funds must be referred to Financial Crime.

name: Financial Crime Function
description: Internal compliance function responsible for receiving and investigating escalations of missing evidence, positive screening results, unclear ownership, and suspicious funds. Acts as the escalation point for account onboarding and review issues.
context: Missing evidence, a positive screening result, unclear ownership, or suspicious funds must be referred to Financial Crime.

name: Account Activation Staff
description: Bank staff responsible for account opening and activation. Under this policy, they are prohibited from activating accounts while evidence gaps, screening issues, or investigations remain open.
context: Staff must not activate the account while the issue is open.

name: Account Evidence Documentation and Retention
description: Control requiring maintenance of ownership evidence, source-of-funds documentation, screening results, risk rating, approver identity, and review date in the account record as an audit trail and compliance safeguard.
context: The account record must retain ownership and source-of-funds evidence, screening results, risk rating, approver, and review date.

name: Account Activation Gate
description: Operational control that prevents account activation until all evidence, screening, and ownership verification issues are resolved and cleared by Financial Crime.
context: Staff must not activate the account while the issue is open.

name: Account Screening Results Retention
description: Requirement to retain and document all AML screening results (sanctions, PEP, adverse media checks) in the account record, with positive results triggering mandatory escalation to Financial Crime.
context: The account record must retain ownership and source-of-funds evidence, screening results, risk rating, approver, and review date.
Missing evidence, a positive screening result, unclear ownership, or suspicious funds must be referred to Financial Crime.

name: New Account
description: Account subject to evidence retention, screening, and activation controls under this policy. The account record must retain all required documentation and screening results before activation is permitted.
context: The account record must retain ownership and source-of-funds evidence, screening results, risk rating, approver, and review date.
Staff must not activate the account while the issue is open.
